best_for: Note takers leaving Evernote or OneNote who want Markdown notes they own, synced through their own Nextcloud, Dropbox or OneDrive, with paid Joplin Cloud as an option rather than a requirement.
description:
Joplin is an open-source note-taking app that Laurent Cozic has developed since 2016. It saves notes in an open format, so you will always have access to them. Its paid sync service, Joplin Cloud, is based in France and falls under European Union privacy law.

A note can hold images, video, audio and PDFs, and you can write math formulas and draw diagrams right inside it. On your phone, snap a photo and save it to a note. With Joplin Cloud you can publish a note to the web and send people the link. If you code, the Extension API lets you write your own scripts and plugins, and a terminal version of Joplin is available too.

points.title: Sync where you like
points.text: Joplin syncs through Joplin Cloud, Nextcloud, WebDAV, S3, Dropbox, OneDrive or a local folder. Sync is something you turn on, so the app also works with notes kept on one machine.

points.title: Encrypted end to end
points.text: Notes can be end-to-end encrypted, so whichever sync service you pick stores only scrambled data.

points.title: Joplin Cloud is the paid line
points.text: Basic is EUR 2.99 a month (2 GB, 10 MB per note), Pro EUR 5.99 (30 GB, 200 MB per note) and Teams EUR 7.99 per user, with lower monthly rates when billed yearly. Sharing your notebooks and email-to-note start at Pro. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Two editors and a clipper
points.text: Write in Markdown or a rich text editor. A web clipper for Chrome and Firefox saves pages or screenshots as notes, and plugins and themes extend the app. Mobile apps exist for Android and iOS.

points.title: Windows has a portable build
points.text: Besides the installer, which here can install per-user or for all users, Joplin offers JoplinPortable.exe that keeps its profile next to the program, handy on a USB stick. The Windows listing keeps 78 versions.

points.title: The Flatpak is unofficial
points.text: Joplin's own Linux download is an AppImage with an install script. The Flathub build is not marked verified by Flathub, and Joplin says support for unofficial packages goes to their maintainers. macOS (12 or later) and Linux list only the current release here.
